\section{First column section}
Body text begins in two-column mode after the full-width front matter. The
opening column is filled with synthetic scholarly prose so a genuine gutter
appears on this page rather than a leftover single stack.

Layout recovery should classify the title and abstract as a full-width band
and the following body as two columns. Extra sentences exist only to occupy
vertical space: mixed-band detection fails when the left column never
fills, because the compiled article then looks single-column.

Repeated recovery notes continue down the first column. Each paragraph
stays narrow enough to wrap inside one column, and none of them mention a
figure yet. The second section heading is placed after enough text that it
starts in the right column on the first page.

Further first-column filler restates that full-width abstract lines must
not bridge the later gutter. Title and abstract stay in a spanning front
band; only the body below that band is two-column text.

Another first-column paragraph records that horizontal cuts must fire at
the skip below the abstract. Without that skip, a full-width abstract line
would keep the x-reach across the whole page and hide the gutter.

\section{Second column section}
More column text precedes a spanning figure band. This right-column block
must be visible beside the first-column paragraphs so band detection sees
a MULTI\_COLUMN strip above the later spanning figure.

A second right-column paragraph keeps the column balanced. After this
page, the article switches to a single-column figure band and then resumes
two-column text, matching the Title, two columns, wide figure, two columns
layout required by the milestone.
